correctness.rationale: The rational Blaschke product expansion after vanishing e1,...,e{k-1} starts at ε^k[e_k z^{n-k}-conj(e_k)z^{n+k}]. The unperturbed Bloch norm has a strict nondegenerate radial maximum at ρ²=(n-1)/(n+1). Uniform C1 expansion on an annulus, radial localization O(ε^k), and angular cosine maximization produce the claimed coefficient (1-ρ²)ρ^{n-1}[(n+k)ρ^k-(n-k)ρ^{-k}]|e_k|. The positivity inequality reduces to strict monotonicity artanh(x)/x. Roots-of-unity plus zero entries realize every 2≤k<n, and fixed-k Taylor expansion gives n³C→4k(k²-1)/(3e). Independently compared the rational derivative of z^{n-k}(z^k−t)/(1−tz^k) with the first-variation coefficient for bounded sample (n,k), not a universal numerical proof.
